Subject: Renewal options — ramping to 3x over 18 months

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the call this morning. Orchard is comfortable committing to a multi‑year deal but wants to avoid being locked into an immediate high commit. We discussed a hybrid approach: year 1 annualized baseline with two staged unlocks tied to usage milestones, and an escape/opt‑out clause if usage growth stalls.

High level asks from my side:
- Can Redwood support a 24‑month term with annualized billing and two 6‑month ramp milestones?
- We need a canary rollout plan so we can burst to Dedicated for traffic spikes but fall back if cost becomes prohibitive.
- Legal wants a narrowly scoped escape clause (performance or go‑to‑market failure) with a 60‑day notice.

Attached a simple usage projection for context (renewal‑playbook v1). Can you share a draft amendment and a proposal with committable numbers? Also include how canary traffic will be routed and costs estimated.

Thanks,
Samira
VP Product, Orchard AI

Samira — thanks for the clear note and the projection doc. I ran this by pricing and legal briefly; we can absolutely structure a hybrid 24‑month term with phased annualized buckets. Draft highlights below and attached: ORK‑AMP‑amendment‑draft‑v1.pdf.

Quick summary:
- Term: 24 months, baseline annualized commit of 250k tokens/month equivalent (annualized billing).
- Ramp milestones: 6 and 12 months from effective date. Milestone 1 unlocks additional 50% capacity; Milestone 2 unlocks another 50% (net 2x by month 12, with burst pool available up to 3x capacity subject to committed burst pricing).
- Canary rollout: We recommend a 2‑week canary window for Dedicated routing (region us‑west). Canary uses a 10% mirrored traffic flow and auto‑rollback if P95 latency or error budget exceeds thresholds. Detailed ops checklist in the renewal milestone calendar.
- Escape clause: Narrowly scoped; eligible only if Orchard discontinues the product line or if rolling 30‑day usage < 40% of baseline and no remediation plan after 60 days. Requires 60‑day written notice.

I've attached estimates and a milestone calendar. Marissa and Jonas are on copy to line up legal/ops language and confirm the invoicing cadence.

Next steps: If you like this shape, Marissa will follow with a legal markup (we can take your suggested language) and our finance team will prepare the proforma invoice. Can you confirm whether Orchard prefers invoicing annualized or quarterly?

Best,
Mateo

Samira / team — looping in legal and finance owners. I pushed a clean redline for the escape clause and added a short operational definition of the canary (see ORK‑AMP‑amendment‑draft‑v1.pdf). Key changes I recommend:

1) Escape clause: tighten the metrics to ensure it cannot be invoked for normal usage variability. Recommended trigger: 90‑day trailing average below 50% of baseline AND documented product sunset OR failure to agree on a remediation plan within 30 days. Notice period remains 60 days.

2) Billing: recommend annualized invoicing with quarterly true‑ups to reduce AP / forecasting friction on Orchard's side. That way Orchard gets predictable FY spend but we reconcile actual usage each quarter and apply credit or debit to the next invoice.

3) Canary ops: added rollback thresholds, telemetry hooks (tracing + token‑level cost alerts) and an ops runbook item to test KV cache warmup.

I attached a marked PDF and an internal checklist. Jonas — can you confirm the Dedicated routing/region fallback latency SLOs we will commit to for the canary? Neha — finance to confirm quarterly true‑up workflow and sample invoice language.
